ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a rectangular house with horizontal side 6 m and vertical side 4 m. The dog is tied at the outside top-left corner of the rectangle with a 10 m rope. Reasoning: From the tie point at the outside top-left corner, the house blocks one quadrant, so the dog can sweep a 270° sector of radius 10 m. Its curved boundary contribution is (3/4)(2π·10) = 15π. If the rope wraps around the 6 m top side to the top-right corner, the remaining rope length is 10 - 6 = 4 m, giving an additional 90° arc of radius 4 m with length (1/4)(2π·4) = 2π. If the rope wraps around the 4 m left side to the bottom-left corner, the remaining rope length is 10 - 4 = 6 m, giving another 90° arc of radius 6 m with length (1/4)(2π·6) = 3π. Wrapping around both adjacent sides uses 6 + 4 = 10 m, so no further curved boundary is added. Total curved boundary length is 15π + 2π + 3π = 20π.

method.method_draft: Identify the tie point as the outside top-left corner of the rectangular house. The dog can first sweep a 270° sector of radius 10 m around the tie point, since the house blocks one quadrant. When the rope wraps around the 6 m top side to the top-right corner, 4 m of rope remains, giving an additional 90° arc of radius 4 m. When the rope wraps around the 4 m left side to the bottom-left corner, 6 m remains, giving an additional 90° arc of radius 6 m. Wrapping around two sides uses all 10 m, so no further curved boundary contributes. Add arc lengths: (3/4)(2π·10)+(1/4)(2π·4)+(1/4)(2π·6)=15π+2π+3π=20π.

method.method_draft: Model the reachable region by its sector areas first, then convert to boundary length. Let the rope length be L=10. Around the original outside corner, the accessible region is a 270° sector of radius L. Around the top-right corner, after using 6 m along the top side, the remaining radius is L-6=4 and only a 90° sector is exposed. Around the bottom-left corner, after using 4 m along the left side, the remaining radius is L-4=6 and only a 90° sector is exposed.
